{{short description|Classification of symplectic toric manifolds}}
In [[differential geometry]], a field of mathematics, '''Delzant's theorem''' provides a complete classification of symplectic [[Toric manifold|toric manifolds]] in term of a special class of [[Polytope|polytopes]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=da Silva |first=Ana Cannas |date=2008 |title=Lectures on Symplectic Geometry |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-540-45330-7 |journal=[[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]] |language=en |publisher=[[Springer Nature|Springer]] |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-45330-7 |issn=0075-8434|author-link=Ana Cannas da Silva|url-access=subscription }}</ref> It was proved by Thomas Delzant in 1988.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Delzant |first=Thomas |date=1988 |title=Hamiltoniens périodiques et images convexes de l'application moment |trans-title=Periodic Hamiltonians and convex images of the moment map |url=http://www.numdam.org/item?id=BSMF_1988__116_3_315_0 |journal=[[Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France]] |language=fr |volume=116 |issue=3 |pages=315–339 |doi=10.24033/bsmf.2100 |issn=0037-9484|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

== Preliminaries ==
A symplectic '''toric manifold''' is a [[Compact space|compact]] [[Connected space|connected]] [[symplectic manifold]] <math>(M^{2n},\omega)</math> together with an [[Effective group action|effective]] [[Hamiltonian action]] of the <math>n</math>-dimensional [[torus]] <math>\mathbb{T}^n = \mathbb{S}^1 \times \ldots \times \mathbb{S}^1</math> on <math>M</math>, with moment map denoted by <math>\mu: M \to \mathbb{R}^n</math>. 

The '''convexity theorem''', proved independently in 1982 by [[Michael Atiyah|Atiyah]] and by [[Victor Guillemin|Guillemin]] and [[Shlomo Sternberg|Sternberg]] using [[Morse theory]], states that the image <math>\mu(M) \subset \mathbb{R}^n</math> is the [[convex hull]] of the images of the fixed points of the <math>\mathbb{T}^n</math>-action. It is therefore a [[convex polytope]], also called the '''moment polytope'''.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Guillemin |first=V. |author-link=Victor Guillemin |last2=Sternberg |first2=S. |author-link2=Shlomo Sternberg |date=1982-10-01 |title=Convexity properties of the moment mapping |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01398933 |journal=[[Inventiones mathematicae]] |language=en |volume=67 |issue=3 |pages=491–513 |doi=10.1007/BF01398933 |issn=1432-1297|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Atiyah |first=M. F. |author-link=Michael Atiyah |date=1982 |title=Convexity and Commuting Hamiltonians |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1112/blms/14.1.1 |journal=[[Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society]] |language=en |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=1–15 |doi=10.1112/blms/14.1.1|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

A '''Delzant polytope''' is a special kind of convex polytope in <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>, satisfying the following three properties 

* it is a [[simple polytope]], i.e. for each vertex <math>x</math>, exactly <math>n</math> edges meet at <math>v</math>; 
* it is a rational polytope, i.e. for each vertex <math>x</math>, the edges at <math>x</math> are of the form <math>x+tu_i^x</math>, with <math>t \geq 0</math> and <math>u_i^x \in \mathbb{Q}</math>;
* it is smooth polytope, i.e. for each vertex <math>x</math>, the corresponding vectors <math>u_i^x</math> form a <math>\mathbb{Z}</math>-basis of <math>\mathbb{Z}^n</math>. 

== Statement ==
'''Delzant's theorem''' states that there is a bijective correspondence between <math>2n</math>-dimensional symplectic toric manifolds (up to torus-equivariant symplectomorphism) and Delzant polytopes in <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>:<math display="block">\{\text{Toric manifolds}\} \leftrightarrow \{\text{Delzant polytopes}\}, \quad (M^{2n},\omega,\mathbb{T}^n,\mu) \mapsto \mu(M).</math>More precisely, the moment polytope of every symplectic toric manifold is a Delzant polytope, every Delzant polytope is the moment polytope of such a manifold, and any two such manifolds with equivalent moment polytopes (up to translations and <math>\mathrm{GL}(n,\mathbb{Z})</math>-transformations) admit a torus-equivariant symplectomorphism between them. The proof of this result is based on [[symplectic reduction]].<ref name=":0" />

== Examples ==

=== Projective spaces ===
The [[complex projective space]] <math>\mathbb{CP}^n</math> is a <math>2n</math>-dimensional toric manifold together with the Fubini-Study symplectic form, the action by <math>\mathbb{T}^n = \mathbb{S}^1 \times \ldots \times \mathbb{S}^1</math> given by<math display="block">(e^{i \theta_1}, \ldots, e^{i \theta_n}) \cdot [z_0 : z_1 : \ldots : z_n] := [z_0 : e^{i \theta_1} z_1 : \ldots : e^{i \theta_n} z_n ],</math>and the moment map<math display="block">\mu: \mathbb{CP}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n, \quad [z_0: z_1 : \ldots : z_n] \mapsto \frac{(|z_1|^2, \ldots, |z_n|^2)}{|z_0|^2 + |z_1|^2 + \ldots + |z_n|^2} .</math>Its associated Delzant polytope is the standard <math>n</math>-[[simplex]] in <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>.

In particular, the case <math>n=1</math> can be identified with the <math>\mathbb{S}^1</math>-action by rotations on <math>\mathbb{CP}^1 \cong \mathbb{S}^2</math>, with moment map given by the height function; its associated Delzant polytope is a segment.

=== Products ===
The Delzant correspondence is compatible with products. For instance, the product <math>\mathbb{S}^2 \times \mathbb{S}^2</math> is a 4-dimensional toric manifold, being the product of two copies of the toric manifold <math>\mathbb{CP}^1 \cong \mathbb{S}^2</math> from above. Its associated Delzant polytope is the product of two segments, i.e. a rectangle in <math>\mathbb{R}^2</math>.

=== Other examples ===
Any [[Hirzebruch surface]] is a 4-dimensional toric manifold; its associated Delzant polytope is a [[right-angled trapezium]].
